Title: Card Idea: The Night is Young

Messages.Author: brandonsantacruz
Messages.Body:
The Night is Young
Master
Untap a minion.

Usable for:
-Responsible bleeding (untap grand prey)
-Cross-table help
-Untap your infernal vampire
-Untap a minion that has been locked-down (i.e. Sensory Deprivation, Vampiric Disease, Derange, etc)
-Create a target for Spirit Marionette (Although I consider this one of the most annoying cards in the game)

Be careful when you fight the monsters, lest you become one.
-Friedrich Nietzsche

Messages.Author: wastaz

How about

The Night is Young
Master
Untap a minion. That minion's controller may choose to cancel this card, if he/she does so that minion does not untap as normal during his/her next untap phase.

Messages.Author: Ohlmann
Messages.Body:
Well, the original idea was to be something helpful, not something detrimental .

Given that I believe the helpful part is too costly even on a trifle, I would put this as a vampire special, something like that :

Tzimisce bob
cap 6

Once per game, during your master phase, target a vampire. Its controller can untap him.

So you have the cool idea of cross table help, not any dirty combo, and not for too much of a cost.

Messages.Author: Azel
Messages.Body:
I don't like it being a master. Too much competition. However, I appreciate the succinct clarity of the original version.

However, outside of Precognizant Mobility, there aren't that many cards that untap another minion, which includes allies or older vampires. Perhaps that might be angle you may want to explore.

Here's an odd one, have you considered making it an Event? The name, "The Night is Young" really does lend itself to such treatment. You could even make something crazy where cross table weirdness can trigger...

The Night is Young
Event
During your turn you may choose a minion. You must receive permission to target when targeting another methuselah's minion. Untap that minion.

There, clean, usable crosstable, doesn't forcibly negate specialized tapping (Anima Gathering, etc), usable before, during, or after a minion phase, etc.

Messages.Author: brandonsantacruz
Messages.Body:
@Ohlmann and Reyda
I think that the flame war can move to another thread or, better yet, end right here.

Back to the card:
The cost of an MPA is something to consider when looking at a Spirit Marionette deck, it's true. All Salubri decks I've seen have a hard time doing anything other than surviving. If all people want to do is blow up others' minions, they will generate table hate and (hopefully) get ganged-up on. There is already a good way to deal with any master card that you don't like: sudden reversal.

So does this card as originally written break the Spirit Marionette archetype? Probably not. You'd need to do play testing to know for sure (as much as you can "know" such a thing in this game). As for Anima Gathering, I've seen it in constructed play exactly zero times. It's not a very strong card in most cases, and probably not worth worrying about.

I'd still be very concerned as to whether anyone would put it in a deck.

Now, in draft, it could easily be an interesting choice. You have the card, you have a limited set of choices, you probably don't have a stack of power-cards competing with it. Totally decent card.

Up against me thinking about a few copies of Villein, Dreams of the Sphinx, Palla Grande, Power Structure, intercept locations, Ecoterrorists (and friends), Wash, Sudden Reversal etc. - I'm not sure it makes the cut in all that many situations.

And while it could certainly be a good card in the right situation, it's not going to be great when you draw it in your opening hand and no-one is really doing anything for several turns. In a frenetic end game when everyone is grinding down pool? Totally cool. When my grand-prey has no vampires (first few turns) or lots of vampires with lots of blood and resources? Not so useful.

If it was something like:
Untap a minion; their controller may cancel this card by burning one pool.
Alternatively, move two blood from the Blood Bank to a vampire; any Methuselah may cancel this card by burning one pool.
...then maybe I could see it making the cut.

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
> brandonsantacruz wrote:
> What about short-leash bleed? Untap your grand prey before bleeding for 5, have an intercept location and/or change of target to reduce the pressure on them when you are inevitably bleeding them. I could see Giovanni and Followers of Set making good use of a card like this.
>
Giovanni power-bleed might conceivably be interested in it for a responsible bleed angle, but the Followers of Set have a better option in Spying Mission - have the bleed succeed, then wipe it out and store up some +bleed for when your grand-prey is your prey.

For the Giovanni, if the grand-prey can declare any sort of block (i.e. at least one minion is untapped - this card could be upping that to two, or from two to three etc.), Tangle Atropos' Hand is potentially more useful for responsible power-bleed. It cancels the action, thus escaping the No Repeat taint, thus allowing you to bleed again. Relatively hard to get hold of, though, and possibly sitting in your Lasombra stealth-bleed deck anyhow.

There's also the school of thought that says "If you're going to bleed irresponsibly, be as irresponsible as you can."
